episodes.203512: A disturbance rotating north around the upper high circulation centered over south central U.S. followed by a backdoor front entering eastern New Mexico in the middle of the week increased monsoon moisture and shower and thunderstorm coverage across the state. Daily slow moving thunderstorms on the Ruidoso burn scars during the afternoon hours resulted in several occurrences flash flooding on and downstream of the burn scars. Slow moving thunderstorms also resulted in flash flooding on the White Sands Missile Range in eastern Lincoln County, near Elk in southwest Lincoln County on July 30th, and in Santa Fe during the evening hours of July 31st with debris flow closing Highway 38 a few miles west of Red River for several hours late on July 31st. Nearby storms also caused a landspout on the West Mesa of Albuquerque and a 73 mph wind gust at Gallup Municipal Airport on July 30th.
episodes.203748: An additional short-wave trough moving through the region along with moist unstable airmass contributed to several days of late afternoon to early evening thunderstorms.
episodes.203762: An upper level wave moving through N CA/NV provided plentiful forcing for storms to develop on July 30. In fact, showers lingered overnight the night before across portions of the Sierra and NE CA. These storms produced robust outflows with multiple areas of blowing dust and one true haboob/dust storm. We also had flooding that closed a roadway that afternoon/evening along US-395 near the Red Rock area.
episodes.203838: Scattered thunderstorms moved across portions of northeast Illinois during the afternoon of July 30th producing heavy rain and one funnel cloud.
episodes.203839: Scattered thunderstorms moved across portions of northwest Indiana during the afternoon of July 30th producing heavy rain.
episodes.203925: A slow moving cold front combined with a highly unstable atmosphere along with tropical moisture to produce slow moving thunderstorms with heavy rainfall. Some of these storms trained over the same areas, resulting in scattered instances of flash flooding. Total rainfall amounts in areas with flash flooding averaged two to four inches.
episodes.203947: Monsoon moisture lead to widespread showers and thunderstorms across southeast Wyoming. A few storms were severe, producing gusty winds, hail, and heavy rain.
episodes.204122: Hot and humid conditions on the 30th combined with a slowly-passing cold front to produce several strong thunderstorms across northern central Indiana.  One cell in Muncie caused wind damage to a school.
episodes.204139: Clusters of thunderstorms, some strong, developed during the late afternoon, lasting into the early evening hours over north Alabama. One of the thunderstorms knocked a tree down in Morgan County creating road blockage.
episodes.204447: Heavy rainfall led to minor flash flooding on the southside of Pueblo and just east of Pueblo Reservoir.
episodes.204448: Heavy rainfall of 1.5-2 inches led to flash flooding around Monument and Black Forest.
episodes.204714: Heavy rain, 1.5 to 3 inches, produced flooding in and around Ypsilanti, Canton, and Northville.
episodes.205101: Hot and humid conditions continued under southwest steering flow. The combination of a moist and unstable airmass triggered diurnal storms, with sea breeze and boundary collisions focused near and east of the Highway 301 corridor into the early evening where storms moved offshore of the local Atlantic coast.
episodes.205102: Hot and humid conditions continued under southwest steering flow. episodes.205123: A moist and unstable summer airmass led to the development of scattered afternoon thunderstorms, a few of which were strong to severe.
episodes.205205: Thunderstorms developed in the Flint Hills into south central Kansas during the evening hours of the 30th then gradually expanded in coverage across much of southern Kansas. The storms continued into the early morning hours of the 31st. These storms produced damaging winds and up to quarter sized hail in south central and southeast Kansas.
episodes.205272: A persistent troughing pattern brought in good instability and shear to produce severe thunderstorms across the region over the 3 day time frame with strong winds as the primary hazard. There was also isolated large hail. Anomalously high moisture content and slower moving storms brought localized flooding. A thunderstorm produced heavy rainfall and caused flooding in Havre and in Clear Creek on the 27th. The Havre airport reported 1.72 inches in about 45 minutes, with other reports in town estimated 2.5 of rain quickly. There were also flooding along Highway 69 & 55 in Jefferson County on the 29th.
episodes.205432: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced a brief severe wind gust that flipped over a boat dock and caused other minor tree damage.
episodes.205433: A weakening thunderstorm complex moved across southcentral Missouri with isolated severe storms producing damaging wind gusts and hail up to half dollars in size. An additional isolated storm moved across Lawrence County and caused wind damage.
episodes.205449: During the early morning of July 30th, a line of thunderstorms moved across eastern Iowa. This line of storms produced damaging winds of 60 to 80 MPH during mainly along and north of Highway 30. This line of storms gradually weakened as it moved eastward. There was isolated hail reported in southeast Iowa.
episodes.205528: Training thunderstorms affected the far northeast Tennessee valley and southwest Virginia on the evening of the 30th, producing some flash flooding across those areas.
episodes.205530: Training thunderstorms affected the far northeast Tennessee valley and southwest Virginia on the evening of the 30th, producing some flash flooding across those areas.
episodes.205543: On the evening of July 29, 2026, a surface front draped from central Nebraska to the state's northeast and southeastern South Dakota, serving as the focal point for thunderstorm development during the late afternoon. As the evening progressed, these storms coalesced into a mesoscale convective complex (MCS) that moved southeast across eastern Nebraska and southwestern Iowa. While the atmosphere was primed with sufficient instability, a lack of shear remained a limiting factor for widespread storm organization. Regardless, several reports of damaging wind gusts ranging from 58 to 70 mph were received throughout the evening. A notable report came from a trained spotter 3 miles west of Westphalia, Iowa, who measured a 70 mph gust. Damage was also reported, including 6- to 8-inch diameter tree limbs downed in Murray, Nebraska.

Given cold temperatures aloft and steep low level lapse rates, one storm was able to become severe and produce a cluster of damaging wind gusts in southern CT.

episodes.205656: A weakness aloft moved across the northern gulf coast interacting with deep moisture. Numerous showers and storms resulted.
episodes.205757: Scattered thunderstorms developed over southwestern Nebraska during the mid afternoon hours of July 29th. Thunderstorms grew upscale over the next couple of hours, becoming widespread across the area by early evening. Heavy rain of 1 to 3 inches fell from Lincoln into Custer County, leading to flash flooding in the North Platte area.

episodes.206104: A cold front moved across Wyoming and brought severe thunderstorms to central portions of the state. The main impact from the storms was large hailin Johnson, Hot Springs, Natrona and Fremont Counties. The largest hail was ping pong ball sized hail in Johnson County to the south of Buffalo. The Natrona County airport near Casper had around a 10 minute period of high wind, with gusts as high as 66 mph.
episodes.206107: A thunderstorm passed over the South Bighorn County airport near Greybull and produced a maximum wind gust of 67 mph.
episodes.206203: A primed microburst environment was in place on July 30, 2025, as hot and humid conditions combined with a weak surface low pressure across southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi. Numerous severe thunderstorms developed through the afternoon. In Marrero, Jefferson Parish, thunderstorm winds knocked down a powerline, while additional wind damage in Hammond brought down multiple trees, including one onto a powerline. In Centreville, MS, a downed tree damaged two homes. Heavy rainfall also led to flash flooding, with high water reported in Gretna, Baton Rouge, and Ascension Parish where parking lots were submerged and a vehicle partially underwater. Hail up to the size of quarters was observed in Baton Rouge.
episodes.206204: A primed microburst environment was in place on July 30, 2025, as hot and humid conditions combined with a weak surface low pressure across southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi. Numerous severe thunderstorms developed through the afternoon. episodes.206229: A morning shower developed just off the Charleston County and Colleton County coast. The environment was supportive of the development of waterspouts and several reports were received from Edisto Island and Seabrook Island.
episodes.206238: Thunderstorms erupted within a very moist and unstable environment across central South Dakota during the afternoon of July 29 in response to an approaching upper level short-wave from Colorado. These thunderstorms quickly grew upscale into a line, producing 55 to 75 mph wind gusts across southeast South Dakota, resulting in isolated tree damage. In addition, prolonged heavy rain resulted in some localized flash flooding across northwest Iowa.
episodes.206258: A severe thunderstorm moved westward into Hereford, AZ with a recorded wind gust of 58 mph and no reported damage.
episodes.206290: High pressure over the region brought a period of hot and humid conditions to portions of northwestern Connecticut on July 29-30, 2025. Maximum heat index values (feels like temperatures) between 95 and 104 degrees were observed in some areas during the afternoon hours on one or multiple days. On July 30, 2025, a couple of thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front during the afternoon hours. One of the storms became severe resulting in downed trees and wires.
episodes.206313: Broad southwesterly flow was in place over the area, which allowed for high terrain thunderstorms to develop. With adequate shear and instability in place, a supercell tornado developed across Teller County, with a landspout tornado within the Wet Mountain Valley in Custer County.
episodes.206394: A few strong thunderstorms occurred across southern Montana, producing gusts up to 74 mph and hail up to 2 inches in diameter.
episodes.206402: Thunderstorms erupted within a very moist and unstable environment across central South Dakota during the afternoon of July 29 in response to an approaching upper level short-wave from Colorado. These thunderstorms quickly grew upscale into a line, producing 55 to 75 mph wind gusts across southeast South Dakota and extreme northeast Nebraska, resulting in isolated tree damage. In addition, prolonged heavy rain resulted in some localized flash flooding across northwest Iowa.

episodes.206404: Thunderstorms erupted within a very moist and unstable environment across central South Dakota during the afternoon of July 29 in response to an approaching upper level short-wave from Colorado. These thunderstorms quickly grew upscale into a line, producing 55 to 75 mph wind gusts across southeast South Dakota and extreme northeast Nebraska, resulting in isolated tree damage.  Weakening storms led to only   isolated large hail in southwest Minnesota.
episodes.206775: Localized heavy rainfall led to flooding in Leesburg.
episodes.207195: A thermal ridge was in place across the area, creating a hot and humid environment that was deeply unstable with MLCAPE of 3000-4500 J/kg even through the overnight hours when storms passed across Iowa. Sub-severe storms developed on the evening of July 29th associated with a stationary boundary that was draped across the state, but with little available shear they were disorganized. Meanwhile, a shortwave riding along the ridge pushed in from the west and reached western Iowa after midnight. This upper level support helped to organize the earlier convection into a line of storms in eastern Iowa while the primary line of storms organized in western Iowa. Both resulted in winds gusting 55-65+ mph as they swept across the state, leaving behind broken and uprooted trees that damaged homes in a couple cases.
episodes.207308: Slow moving thunderstorms with rainfall rates as high as 5 inches per hour caused localized flooding in the City of Radford and neighboring Montgomery County.  Heavy rain also caused flooding and a landslide in and around the Town of Rich Creek, VA.
episodes.207541: On July 29th, southwest flow aloft worked to advect mid-level moisture across eastern Oregon. During the afternoon, an embedded shortwave in the flow allowed for scattered thunderstorms to develop. The afternoon Boise sounding showed a dry boundary layer, allowing for the possibility of severe wind gusts.
